content.title: URJ Statement on AIPAC, Campaign Rhetoric, and Antisemitism
content.text: April 13, 2026 - We are deeply concerned by efforts to single out AIPAC as a particularly malign influence in campaign finance. Amidst elevated rhetoric and global tension, political candidates are facing new and significant pressures when it comes to taking positions related to Israel, including whether to accept support from pro-Israel PACs. Every candidate has the right to accept or reject funding from any PAC, including AIPAC’s, but the harsh language being used by some to denigrate and vilify AIPAC borders on – and in some instances crosses over into – antisemitism. Among these efforts was a coordinated campaign targeting AIPAC at the recent DNC gathering, which appeared to be an attempt to marginalize Israel rather than oppose specific policies of the Israeli government. We are pleased that this effort failed.Just as one can oppose AIPAC in good faith, one can oppose and forcefully criticize specific Israeli policies and still support a democratic, pluralistic, Jewish state of Israel and a strong U.S.-Israel relationship. This is a position we have taken on numerous policies and actions of the Israeli government. One can also support all of those things and choose not to accept funds from AIPAC. But to single out and disproportionately demonize AIPAC as a distinctively harmful dark-money entity crosses the line into antisemitic tropes about sinister Jewish political influence.Until such time as congress reforms the nation’s broken campaign finance system overall – an effort we would enthusiastically welcome – to single out AIPAC’s activity will continue to raise questions of antisemitic motivation. We urge candidates, legislators, and all people to heed these concerns and act accordingly. Explore Jewish Life and Get Inspired
